$comment: TF-C119 runtime witness for `snprintf` on all three legs, and the FIRST example in the tree able to pin the UCRT `_Options` bit at all. WHAT IT WITNESSES: stdio.json ships `snprintf` split the same way `sprintf` is -- elf/macho import the real libc symbol, pe64 carries `synthesize: "snprintf"` because there is NO pe symbol to import. MEASURED: `objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll` (2,484 exports) exports NEITHER `snprintf` NOR `__stdio_common_vsnprintf`; it has `__stdio_common_vsprintf` (ordinal 117) and `__stdio_common_vsnprintf_s` (115), and the `_s` twin is a different function, not a spelling variant. msvcrt.dll (the control) exports `_snprintf`/`_vsnprintf`/`vsnprintf`/`sprintf` but STILL not bare `snprintf` -- so unlike the other five printf-family shims, `snprintf` was never importable on pe under EITHER CRT. The synthesized body therefore reuses `sprintf`'s core, `__stdio_common_vsprintf`, adding NO new import at all (verified: the pe64 import table of a snprintf-using binary lists only the three `__stdio_common_v*` cores that were already there), and differs in exactly two arguments -- `_Options` = STANDARD_SNPRINTF_BEHAVIOR (bit 1) instead of sprintf's legacy bit 0, and `_BufferCount` = the caller's REAL n instead of the `(size_t)-1` unbounded sentinel -- plus the header's `r < 0 ? -1 : r` clamp. WHY THIS EXAMPLE EXISTS RATHER THAN LEANING ON shipped_sprintf_ucrt: that example states its own limit -- with an unbounded `_BufferCount` no truncation is reachable, so `_Options` 0, 1 and 2 yield byte-identical output AND an identical return, making a wrong bit INVISIBLE there. It named the missing piece: "pinning _Options properly needs a bounded-buffer consumer (snprintf), not yet shipped." This is that consumer. THE PINS ARE THE EXACT DIVERGENCE POINTS between the candidate behaviours, every one of which is SILENT (none errors, none fails to link). TWO INDEPENDENT WRONG-ARGUMENT FAILURES ARE COVERED and BOTH RED-ON-DISABLE RUNS WERE MEASURED, not asserted -- flipped in synth_stdio_shim.cpp, rebuilt, run on pe64, then restored and re-run green. (a) `_Options` CLEARED (1<<1 -> 0), i.e. the pre-C99 `_snprintf`: the corpus example goes exit 42 -> exit 50 with EMPTY stdout, failing check 1 because the legacy core returns -1 where C99 requires the would-be length 5; a standalone probe shows the same flip verbatim, `snprintf(buf,4,"%d",12345)` giving `A ret=5` -> `A ret=-1`. ★ HONEST SCOPE, because the obvious second claim did NOT reproduce: legacy `_snprintf` is documented to leave the buffer unterminated too, but on the ucrtbase build measured it still wrote the NUL at buf[3] with the bit clear -- so the RETURN VALUE is this bit's only observed discriminator, and NUL placement is deliberately not claimed as one. (b) `_BufferCount` replaced by the `(size_t)-1` unbounded sentinel: exit 42 -> exit 51, failing check 2 because the core writes the whole "12345\0" past the 4 bytes the caller promised, putting '4' at buf[3]; check 3's sentinel byte at buf[4] covers the same fault from the other side. This is the more dangerous of the two and NOTHING in checks 1/4/5/7 can see it, because it corrupts memory rather than text. Restoring each flip returned the example to exit 42. CHECK 8 is specific to this recipe's SHAPE: every previously shipped stdio shim has at most two named parameters before the `...`, but snprintf has three (buf, n, fmt), so the body must derive `ap` at home-slot index 3 -- an off-by-one there reads the format pointer or the count as the first vararg, and the FP operand additionally requires its xmm value be spilled to its own positional home slot, which no integer check can see. ANTI-FOLD: every operand AND every buffer size is read from a mutable global, and checks 9's operands are DERIVED AT RUNTIME from a previous snprintf's return value -- a value no pass can know without modelling the C runtime -- so the `release` shippedPipeline arm cannot precompute these strings and reduce the example to a no-op. The same source runs on every target listed below, so it is also a cross-target agreement check; MEASURED, pe64 and elf64-x86_64 produce byte-identical results. ★★ THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO DARWIN ARM HERE, AND ITS ABSENCE IS PAIRED TO A DESCRIPTOR ROW — the two land TOGETHER or not at all. stdio.json gates `snprintf` to `availableObjectFormats: ["elf"]` because that libSystem exports it is INFERRED (from `_sprintf`/`_printf`/`_fprintf` already being eager-imported by every macho binary that loads and runs on real Apple Silicon, TF-C113) and NOT MEASURED: the operator's Mac was unreachable and no macOS SDK or .tbd stub exists on the build host. Under the eager-import law a wrong guess breaks EVERY macho binary's LOAD, not just the ones calling snprintf, so the row follows the same staging its own file applies to `popen`/`pclose` and `fileno` — macho stays fail-loud S0001 until a real run witnesses the export. A `macho64-arm64-darwin-exec` arm against an `[elf]`-gated row would fail loud `S0001 ... got snprintf` and red the suite, so declaring one here now would just be a broken half of the pair. ⇒ WHEN THE MAC RUN HAPPENS: add `"macho"` to stdio.json's `snprintf` row AND restore the arm `{"spec": "arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec", "artifact": "main", "runOn": ["darwin"], "emulator": "", "expectedStdout": "mix=20|a\nwould=10 back=2\n"}` below, in ONE edit. That run is the measurement this session could not take; it is scheduled as the last step before this PR merges. exit = 42.
